thread.title: Apple stock price target gets a big boost at Goldman; analyst eats his hat about iPhone demand - MarketWatch

author: Tomi Kilgore
title: Apple stock price target gets a big boost at Goldman; analyst eats his hat about iPhone demand - MarketWatch
text: Goldman Sachs analysts said Apple Inc. AAPL, +0.54% has made them "eat our hat," as the cautious stance they took over the summer has proved wrong. Lead analyst Rod Hall raised his stock price target to $240, which is about 7.4% above current levels, from $164. He kept his rating at neutral. The stock was up 0.2% in afternoon trade, after pulling back 2.3% over the past two sessions from Tuesday's record close of $228.36, but had still run up 32% year to date. Since Hall downgraded Apple to neutral on Feb. 6, the stock has soared 37% while the Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA, -0.22% has gained 3.8%. The reason Hall changed his view ahead of Apple's iPhone launch event on Sept. 12, he had expected worse iPhone X demand and some pullback in the stock during the summer, but iPhone demand remained healthy and the stock kept climbing. The better-than-expected demand leads him to believe Apple is unlikely to go for lower price points on the iPhones, which would be "potentially positive" for average selling prices and earnings. Piper Jaffray also raised its stock price target Friday, going to $250 from $218.
